correctness.rationale: Enumerating centered balls yields, after removing a common nonnegative baseline, the map F_i(x)=max(x_i,x_i/2,mu)-max(0,mu) with mu=sum(x_i)/(m+1). Its strict affine-cell ℓ1 Jacobian columns are bounded by 2m/(m+1): for mu>0 only direct or mean-selected leaves occur, with sums 1+(s-2)/(m+1) or s/(m+1); for mu<0 the center selects zero and at most m-1 leaves can choose the mean (otherwise summing x_i/2<mu contradicts mu<0), giving at most 1+(m-1)/(m+1). Continuity handles ties. A strict witness with hub=3, first leaf=3+(m-1)/2 and other leaves=2, perturbing first leaf, attains 2m/(m+1), and m=1 reduces to x/2. For signed absolute-value averages f=(1,-1,...,-1), g=(2,epsilon,0,...,0) have input TV epsilon but output TV m-epsilon/2, forcing divergence. Independently reproduced rational equality for m<=16, 5600 rational pair bounds; these bounded examples are not an infinite proof.
